messages:
Priya (AE): quick heads-up 12: Customer Z wants a capacity plan tied to their 12mo commit. Targets: 150 rps steady, p99 <=200ms, seq ~256, occasional 1k rps spikes for ~20 mins. They require eu-west + us-east and private deployment option. Need reserved recommendations + autoscale/fallback and cost scenarios.
Evan (SE): got it. couple clarifying q's: are their spikes uniform across users or short-lived bursts? and tolerance for quantized fallback?
Priya (AE): spikes can be sudden (promo events). they're open to quantized fallback for up to 20% of traffic if quality checks pass.
Lou (SalesOps): pricing context: reserved GPU SKUs available at 6/12/24mo. We should present 2 pricing options: conservative reserved (cover 60% steady + buffer) vs aggressive reserved (cover steady+half burst). Also call out one-time private setup fee.
Evan (SE): quick perf math: redwood-7b-opt ~5k tokens/s per A100-80GB under realistic batching at seq256. With 150 rps * avg 120 tokens = 18k tokens/s ~ need ~4 GPUs baseline if each 4.5k tokens/s. For safety and headroom propose reserved=5. For 1k rps pure reserved would need ~30 GPUs. So recommend reserved 5 + autoscale to 20 with burst credits and prewarmed slots.
Kai (SRE): autoscale proposal: reserved=5, prewarm=5 (warm workers to handle fastest spin-ups), max=20, scale_step=3, cooldown=20s. Fallback chain: 1) route to redwood-7b-quant (if quality gates pass), 2) degrade to redwood-3b for low-priority traffic. Include region failover: route eu overflow to us-east if eu saturated? check compliance.
Kai (SRE): sample config snippet:

```
autoscale:
  reserved: 5
  prewarm: 5
  max: 20
  step: 3
  cooldown: 20s
fallbacks:
  - id: redwood-7b-quant
    threshold_p99_ms: 250
    percent_traffic: up-to-30%
  - id: redwood-3b
    when: non-critical
```

Maya (CS): security note: private deployment requires KMS integration and audit logs. that'll add 2-3 weeks to onboarding and an addendum to the T&Cs. Customer also asks for isolation matrix for their security questionnaire. I'll own that and work with infra.
Lou (SalesOps): I'll prepare two cost sheets: (A) reserved 5 GPUs + autoscale to 20 with burst credits; (B) reserved 10 GPUs + smaller autoscale. Need exact hourly costs from infra team.
Evan (SE): monitoring/alerts to recommend: p99 > 200ms, token throughput drop >10%, queue depth > 50ms, and autoscale failures. Also advise enabling per-request tracing for billing reconciliation (small perf penalty). Call that out.
Priya (AE): can we generate a one-pager showing recommended sizing, cost scenarios, failover, and SLAs? need by tomorrow for their EPM review.
Kai (SRE): infra-bot starting a synthetic prewarm test for 20 GPUs at 1000rps at 16:00 UTC. job_id: prewarm-1946. I'll post results here.
infra-bot: prewarm job started job_id=prewarm-1946 target_gpus=20 sim_rps=1000 est_duration=12m
Lou (SalesOps): thumbs up. i'll align on pricing language (committed vs burst billing) and include private deployment fees.
infra-bot: prewarm job complete job_id=prewarm-1946 summary: sustained 1000rps with 30% requests on quantized fallback. q99 tail: 260ms; p95: 140ms. full report: https://redwood.internal/bench/prewarm-1946
Evan (SE): thanks. folding these numbers into the one-pager. note: during quantized fallback q99 slips to ~260ms so mention SLAs conditional on fallback.
Maya (CS): I'll start the isolation matrix doc and security questionnaire answers. flagging legal for contractual addendum.
Priya (AE): great team. once one-pager and Lou's pricing are ready we'll send to customer. tagging follow-ups: @Maya (CS) isolation matrix, @Kai (SRE) final autoscale config, @Evan (SE) perf caveats and bench links.
Lou (SalesOps): will share pricing spreadsheets.
Priya (AE): end of thread.
